siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|2|ה: "Everything as a spring." — it implies even those places where the river did not originally flow; and so Ran in the name of Rambam (not as Darkei Moshe wrote that Rambam holds like Maharik below). And he wrote, end of his words: however, the testimony of R' Eliezer ben Tzadok (who testified about flowing waters that increased upon trickling waters that they are valid and purify in flowing waters) even according to this view (of Rambam) certainly implies that even where the river widened he refers, for if it only referred where the river ran along, it would be obvious — would three drops invalidate this river? end of his words. But Maharik wrote in root 115 that even if flowing waters are a majority they purify only where it originally flowed; and so it appears Ra'avad ruled in Hilchot Mikveh that he established, end of his words; and Beit Yosef rejected his words, for Ra'avad's view is the opposite, and this is not a valid challenge, for Ra'avad in Ba'alei Nefesh, daf 66 side a, brings "there is one who holds so" and it was not clear to Maharik whether Ra'avad argues or not; then Beit Yosef wrote further from Rabbenu Shimshon, Rosh, and Mordechai one can also prove like Ran, and not like Maharik, for they wrote, etc., until before Rabbenu Yerucham and Maharik, end of his words; and Magen Avraham followed him, daf 311 side a, and I did not understand his words, for on the contrary from Rosh, Rosh, and Mordechai one can prove like Maharik and not like Ran; if like Ran, what is difficult for them? It is obvious, for Ran already answered that even where it did not originally flow it purifies in flowing waters; rather certainly like Maharik, that even though flowing waters are a majority it does not purify where it did not originally flow. And it appears that even according to Rabbenu Tam and his supporters below who permit even with a majority of trickling waters, that is only where it originally flowed; but where it widened, even Rabbenu Tam concedes even if flowing waters increased, and so it implies explicitly in Rabbenu Yerucham.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|8|ב: "And if the spring," etc. — meaning, most of the spring passes into the vessel and a bit passes and sprays at the lip of the vessel; since a few days of the spring did not pass through the vessel at all, they raise the abundant water and purify the drawn water, and even though they return and mix, all have the law of a spring (and see Beit Yosef what he wrote for the view of Rashba, and R' Yosef Tayitzak already challenged him, and Bach — however, what Bach wrote on Beit Yosef and upheld his words from the language of Rashba's responsum, etc., and one immerses on its back and outside, as we learned, etc., and it is a great wonder, etc., that an error escaped him that the word "and outside" attaches to "one immerses," and it is like Beit Yosef's view, not like Bach who understood that "outside" attaches above, and therefore he strained needlessly to emend Rashba's words — this is clear and there is no need to extend here in these words, since for the law the Mechaber himself ruled that spraying on the lip of the vessel is required, and it is simple) and Bach wrote: however, what Rashba permits to immerse inside the vessel when there are forty se'ah between them is a novel law and does not imply so from the poskim; rather inside the vessel is always invalid unless pierced in its base, even if there are forty se'ah between the spring and the vessel; and also from the language of Rosh himself it appears he did not decide this law, if so. Beit Yosef wrote in the name of Mordechai in the name of R' Yoel and in the name of Rokeach that drawn water that was drawn through a channel in the ground to a large barrel holding more than forty se'ah, and the barrel was sunk in the ground — it is forbidden to immerse inside the barrel, etc., even though the barrel-water, which is drawn, is connected to the channel — if so; and it is straightforward that if there is in the base of the barrel a hole like the opening of a wineskin, it is valid.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|10|ב: "To have for it the law of a mikveh." — it does not purify except in forty se'ah and in ashboran — Tur. Maharik wrote, roots 115 and 196, that specifically where the water rested in the mikveh and already became ashboran; but where it has not yet rested and is still flowing, even though the spring was stopped, the law of a spring is upon them, for its vitality has not ceased since it flows; and proof from a wave that was uprooted (above, seif 5). And even though here the law of mikveh is upon them because the pool was full of water — but if the pool was empty and filled from the spring, even though the spring was stopped, the law of a spring is upon it, end of his words. But the view of Ra'avad that he brought there is that in every case the law of mikveh is upon it; and so Rashba in Sha'ar HaMayim that Beit Yosef brought — nevertheless the law of mikveh is upon it; and so implies the plain sense of the mishnah and poskim that there is no distinction; and so is proven in Perishah who explained Tur's words regarding an empty pool and an uprooted wave — there is no proof, for that case is different, for there the wave uprooted itself and its vitality is great, and it also uprooted from the sea itself, and likewise its manner of flowing even though uprooted, unlike here. Also what Maharik brought there as proof — otherwise it would be difficult for one who invalidates (below, seif 50) when they exit through a crack that mishnah of three mikvaot (below, seif 55), for there the water exited on the lip of the mikveh — rather certainly there it deals with a spring that was stopped, end of his words; and Beit Yosef brings it below, beginning of daf 248 — I do not recognize this proof for several reasons. One, that there it deals with three mikvaot that are springs that purify in flowing waters — know that even for Maharik who establishes it regarding a spring, nevertheless he holds that in such a case it is a complete spring; if so, these three mikvaot are springs. And further, and this is primary: there there are no flowing waters at all, for flowing applies only when they flow by themselves; and likewise in a crack the water flows by itself through the crack and goes and does not return to flow; but those that exited on the lip of the mikveh through the power of the person immersing — through this they were filled and exited on their lips, and when the immerser leaves they return to their first place — certainly in such a case they are not flowing waters; and so is in responsum of Rivash, beginning of siman 292, explicitly, who brings there that mishnah of three mikvaot and wrote they are not called flowing waters even though the water will not remain in the place one immerses, rather it is called ashboran since it comes from the mikveh and to it they return, only it was diminished by necessity through a person or something else in the mikveh, etc., end of his words; and so too the Rav below, seif 50, even regarding a crack in a mikveh where they return there they are not called flowing waters. And further, there the mikvaot mix with each other through the water that exited on their lips, and there is no flowing here but mixture of mikvaot; therefore the essence is that when the spring was stopped there is no spring upon it even in flowing waters, rather it has the law of trickling waters.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|11|א: "And nevertheless," etc. — in Sefer Magen Avraham he wondered: why in seif 10, when the spring continues, it purifies in flowing waters? And it appears to him that there it deals when the trickling waters did not increase — and it is simple.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|11|ב: "Only in ashboran," etc. — and accordingly one must say that above, seif 8, that if it sprays on the lip of the vessel it is permitted outside it even if the water inside is abundant — that is specifically in ashboran; but the plain sense of the words there appears that the law of a spring is upon them for every matter; and so implies from Bach and other acharonim. And one can distinguish, for there is different since the water itself inside the vessel is also from the spring and now the spring still sprays into them and they are connected to the spring — unlike here — examine.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|12|א: "A spring," etc. — it is written in Hagahat Drishah: it must be that the spraying from the spring was stopped, for otherwise it would not have the law of mikveh but the law of a spring; and it is not clear, for even if the spraying was not stopped it has the law of mikveh (since they carried it over the backs of vessels, it is as if stopped), as implies from the poskim; and see Beit Yosef, siman 198.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|12|ג: "It returned to be," etc. — it is written in Tosafot Yom Tov, chapter 5, mishnah 2: it appears to me that here too it deals when without these vessels the water would pass; for if not so, say thus: they would be invalidated even for a mikveh because their formation requires taharah, as Rosh wrote (below, seif 35) regarding setting up handles — end of his words; and I did not know from Rosh's words proof that Rosh said so only for rainwater, but not for a spring that was drawn, as below, seif 49; and so too in Hagahat Perishah, seif 40, that here in every case it is permitted since it is a spring; however below, seif 49, the Mechaber brought: there is one who does not distinguish in this.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|12|ד: "Provided he does not immerse," etc. — for we decree on account of inside the vessel — Rosh. And above, siman 198, Tur and Beit Yosef brought in the name of Ra'avad and other poskim that specifically with vessels that receive tumah does this decree apply, unlike earthenware and the like that do not receive tumah; and Beit Yosef challenged there Tur for writing that Rosh, may he rest in peace, did not distinguish in this. And it appears to me that Tur holds according to Rosh that Rabbi Yosi decreed only l'chatchila but not b'dieved, and even for earthenware he decreed l'chatchila lest one come to immerse inside the vessel; for if Rosh held to distinguish thus he should have written that Rabbi Yosi's reason is since it is a vessel that receives tumah he decreed on account of its inside; and from the fact that the plain statement of Rabbi Yosi is "we decree on account of inside the vessel," apparently he decreed for all vessels; nevertheless this is specifically l'chatchila, but b'dieved it is permitted, for we did not forbid in the Gemara (and above, siman 198, 131) even in a valley except because of modesty — apparently b'dieved is permitted. Also in Rava's statement Rosh wrote: a woman should not stand on a vessel or a wooden depression and immerse because of modesty, and omitted earthenware; and if Rosh held to distinguish he should not have omitted it, from which we learn as Ra'avad wrote that specifically for earthenware there is no decree of bathhouses; rather certainly he does not distinguish, and Rabbi Yosi deals with l'chatchila — and therefore Tur wrote here plainly "provided he does not immerse on the backs of vessels," implying even earthenware, and this is l'chatchila. And accordingly it would appear to be lenient b'dieved for all vessels; but since the view of Ra'avad, Rashba, Ran, and Beit Yosef above, siman 198, is to forbid even b'dieved on other backs of vessels, and so explained above, siman 198, seif 31, one should not be lenient; but for earthenware one may be lenient b'dieved, for both according to the one view and the other view it is permitted, as stated.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|14|א: "Such as when one placed it near a trickling spring," etc. — behold they are valid. And there flowing waters are upon them, for it is like descending in spraying without interruption; and see above, seif 48, s.k. 103.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|14|ב: "Valid." — for the walnut shell on which he sits is not considered like vessels — there.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|15|א: "And a spring," etc. — or a spring in any quantity. And Beit Yosef wrote in the name of responsum of Ramban, siman 231, that a spring in any quantity, even if standing, such as these mikvaot whose water is from spring sources — even though its water is little, it is not invalidated by increase of drawn water; and so implies from the words of other poskim.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|15|ג: "Even though they are many," etc. — and Beit Yosef wrote in the name of Rambam and Rosh: however, from the spring the law of flowing waters was nullified, rather it purifies only in ashboran; and so Bach for Tur's view, and so Darkei Moshe for Tur's view, and he brings it in Hagahat Drishah, seif 25; and the Rav already explained this in seif 11. And nevertheless it is clear that the law of a spring is upon it for immersion of vessels in any quantity, and the Mechaber did not explain this, that it is a spring for immersion of vessels in any quantity; and so in several places in this siman, such as seifim 2, 5, 10, 11, and other places, he should have explained and did not — because since tumah and taharah are not practiced among us, immersion of vessels nowadays is not relevant; and for vessels taken from idolaters, in truth we hold that forty se'ah are also required like a person, as explained at the beginning of siman 120 — see there.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|15|ד: "And see above, seif 40," etc. — meaning that there it is explained that there are disputants: in a spring of any quantity that does not have forty se'ah, drawn water invalidates it — see there.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|15|ה: "Three log," etc. — and both at the beginning (meaning there was drawn water at first in the pit and afterward mikveh-water) and at the end (drawn water fell after mikveh-water) it is not invalidated except by three log — so too Beit Yosef in the name of the poskim; and so ruled the acharonim.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|15|ו: "The language 'he wrings his garment and lifted it,'" etc. — meaning the mikveh lacked forty se'ah then; when he immerses and lifts his garment, the water in his garment becomes drawn and invalidates the lacking mikveh if there are three log in it; but when he did not lift the garment, since the water in the garment comes from this mikveh and is still connected to it, it did not become drawn.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|15|ז: "He wrings his garment," etc. — Beit Yosef in the name of responsum of Ramban, siman 231, in the name of Ra'avad: the reason is since the water descends to the mikveh from a person's hands. According to this he answered that above, seif 7, in a vessel pierced in its base it does not invalidate the mikveh, and a garment here is like a pierced vessel; and he wrote: and since so, even in a pierced vessel, whatever fell from a person's hand drawing to the mikveh invalidates the mikveh; and they only said it does not invalidate when they fall by themselves from a pierced vessel to the mikveh, for since they exited through its piercing from the category of vessel and fall by themselves to the mikveh, it is valid — end of his words. And Bach wrote, siman 221: and it appears to me from precision of his language that specifically when the person intends to draw to cast into the mikveh there it invalidates; but if they fell from his hand unintentionally, it is as if they fell by themselves not through a person and they do not invalidate, etc. According to this he strained to reconcile that of one who removes mud to the sides, etc.; but to me it appears the opposite from precision of his language: whatever comes from a person's hand, even unintentionally, invalidates; and specifically when they fell by themselves from a pierced vessel to the mikveh is it valid; and so appears from Ba'alei Nefesh to Ra'avad, daf 69 side a, and the case of removing mud fits its plain sense — see there; and Beit Yosef brings it below nearby. But it is difficult, for Tur and the Rav and other poskim wrote below, end of seif 40, that one who draws from a mikveh and fears lest they return from the vessel with which they draw water — three log to another mikveh after forty se'ah were lacking and will invalidate it — pierce the vessel in its base and then they are not considered drawn water; and what of it — in the end through a person, even by itself, is invalid? One can say it is different there, since he draws water from there, if so he certainly does not want the water to fall there, for on the contrary he draws them from there and it is by itself — examine. Taz wrote: some say specifically when they flow by themselves from the garment to the mikveh they are not called drawn; but if he squeezed them in his hands, even though the garment is still partly in the mikveh, they are drawn and invalid, etc. And in Ma'adanei Melech, daf 307, he wrote he did not know who these "some say" are; and he understood he intended for Ramban in the name of Ra'avad above that Beit Yosef brings at the end of daf 237; and therefore he challenged him, for their view is opposite; and it appears to me he intended for Rokeach that Beit Yosef brings below, this siman, daf 246, beginning of side 4, and so it is: and it implies their essence is that he lifted it from inside it; but Rokeach wrote "lifted from inside it" meaning squeezed with hands from it — end of his words; it appears from his words that even though he did not lift it, since water exited through squeezing, they invalidate the mikveh — end of his words, Beit Yosef; and see below, seif 63.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|15|י: "In an alternative case," etc. — this is the mishnah's explanation: in an alternative case, when he did not intend to increase, etc.; but Rambam and Beit Yosef explained: he intended — when he casts that drawn water into the mikveh, he intends to increase the mikveh-water so there be water in abundance and it not lack through immersions in it; then they combine. And so explained R' Ovadiah of Bartenura; and so too Tosafot Yom Tov; and Bach wrote that R' Ovadiah of Bartenura explained: he intended to increase vessels — and this is one explanation; perhaps a different book was before him. And in the name of Rashba in Sha'ar HaMayim, Beit Yosef brought: in an alternative case, when they fell there unintentionally; but if he placed them there intentionally, even from ten vessels and even after much time, they combine and invalidate it — if so.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|20|א: "And the channel enters," etc. — Rosh explained: this is a channel of rainwater; and Beit Yosef explained: if it were a spring it would purify the drawn water in the pit in any quantity, as above, seif 11; and so he wrote in the name of Ra'avad. And it deals when there are not forty se'ah in the channel — for if so, behold the pit is purified through hashakah, as below, seif 52; and so in Tosafot Yom Tov, chapter 3, mishnah 3, in the name of Rosh and Rosh; and see above, seif 60.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|22|א: "The mikveh was," etc. — and it deals with a mikveh that holds only forty se'ah; therefore we say that water coming upon it pushes the water within it; but if it held more than that, it is possible the invalidated water remained and the water coming upon it too — and it is simple. Agudah, beginning of Mikvaot: from here it would appear to me that when they empty a mikveh and it was invalidated by three log of drawn water, if they remove from it a bit more than was in it when the three log fell in, it is valid; but I did not see my teachers practice so; and perhaps one can distinguish between when the water exited by itself and when they drew and removed from it; and I discussed before my teachers to validate it if they did not remove all the water and dried the mikveh with cloths or sand, or pierced the vessels drawing in it to remove it from the category of vessel — see in Semag and Semak; and there are those who ruled that a spring is not invalidated by three log of drawn water, and they extended in proofs, and I did not see many practice so — end of his words; and see above, seif 40, in the hagahah.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|22|ב: "The mikveh was," etc., "less than three log and they completed it," etc. — here, even if the mikveh is very large, it is valid; for even though less than three log remained in it, nevertheless it was not invalidated, only not validated; and therefore we say the less than three log are as if they are not, and the rainwater afterward validates it; and so is Beit Yosef's intent also; and Bach in seif 27 wrote on this and did not examine, etc., and his words are astonishing.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|22|ג: "They did not invalidate it," etc. — and specifically with valid water; but with impure water, whatever lacks from the mikveh more than a kortov — which is the weight of a dinar — Rambam wrote they invalidate it unless valid rainwater afterward increased upon it; however Ra'avad and Rosh argue that in every case less than three log does not invalidate the mikveh, as explained in Beit Yosef — see there; and so appears the view of Tur and the Mechaber.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|23|_: Wine, etc., does not invalidate it. And it is explicit in the words of Rosh that specifically when they did not change the appearance of the mikveh; but if they changed its appearance they invalidated it — and it is straightforward, end of his words, Beit Yosef; and so Taz; and it is straightforward that even if there are forty se'ah in the mikveh and its appearance changed, it is invalid, as below, seif 25, 26.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|24|א: "They do not invalidate," etc. — and Rambam, chapter 7, wrote: beer is among those that invalidate and do not combine; and Beit Yosef brings it.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|24|ב: "Thirty-nine se'ah." — and the same law: lacking a kortov they do not complete; only he informs us that even lacking a se'ah they do not invalidate.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|24|ג: "But in drawn water," etc. — and Rambam's view is that in drawn water, only up to the majority is valid; and Beit Yosef brought Rashbatz who wrote so in the name of Ra'avad; and he wrote: even though the acharonim agreed to validate — nevertheless one should not put his head into the dispute — end of his words.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|25|ב: "But," etc., "wine," etc. — even not as drawn water, such as wine drawn into it from the press and lees from the olive press not through vessels — Ra'avad — see there.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|25|ג: "In the quantity it was." — even though it did not change to the appearance of wine, it is invalid since it changed from the appearance of water that was at first — Ra'avad.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|30|א: "But snow," etc. — specifically when placed in the mikveh while still snow; but if it melted and became water before being placed in the mikveh, behold it is like other water and invalidates the mikveh; and so in Beit Yosef; and it is straightforward.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|30|ב: "And not more in it." — see in Beit Yosef who wrote that all poskim hold one may immerse in snow if there are forty se'ah in it; and we conclude; and nevertheless one should not be lenient to act against a d'oraisa prohibition against R' Eliezer and Rabbi Shimcha; however to immerse one's hands in snow to eat if he has no water, since netilat yadayim is d'rabbanan, it appears one may rely on R' Shmarya since the plain words of the mishnah and poskim support him; and he wrote what Rambam wrote: even if one brought forty se'ah of snow at first and placed them in a depression and crushed them there, behold it is a complete valid mikveh — "and crushed" means he pressed its hollow; end of his words (and so Bach, that Rambam's view is to permit immersing in snow as it is). And this requires further study, for in Beit Yosef, siman 165, he wrote that "crushed" means until they become water specifically; and therefore he wrote in Shulchan Aruch there, seif 12: snow, hail, and frost, etc., if one crushed them until they became water one may take from them and immerse, etc., and the matters contradict each other — requires further study. And for practical halachah, requires further study, for what Beit Yosef wrote that poskim permit does not exist, for Ra'avad and Rashi forbid and Beit Yosef and Bach bring them; also Razah forbids and Beit Yosef brings him; and Rambam appears to forbid too, for "crushed" means until they become water, and therefore he wrote "crushed" at the end and did not write so at the beginning regarding "bringing up," rather he holds like Ra'avad and Rashi: for completion only he completes as it is, but not entirely snow; and so Rambam, chapter 21 of Hilchot Shabbat: one does not crush snow so its water flows — Gemara, end of chapter Bameh Madlikin; apparently crushing snow means it became water; and Rosh too possibly holds so, for he did not write it helps even if it did not melt, only for completion; and so in Chiddushei Agur in the name of Rosh; and you will not find any posek explicitly that immersion in entirely snow is valid except R' Shmarya who is lenient, and those after him already argued, as in Mordechai; and so ruled Beit Chadash to forbid. Again I found in Maharil in Hilchot Tevilah, and so it is: Mahari Segal said: it is stated in the Gemara that one would force his wife to immerse in a pile of snow in the rainy season, and such is the halachah — end of his words; and it appears these words are not a support and it is recognizable that some hasty student wrote them, for he wrote "it is stated in the Gemara" and it is not in the Gemara, rather the incident is in Mordechai, end of chapter Bameh Madlikin, who came before R' Shimon and he ruled so to permit, and his colleagues already argued with him, and R' Shimon himself retracted, as in Mordechai there — see there.
siftei-kohen/part-001.txt|30|ג: "He presses its hollow." — that he estimates when it melts and becomes water, for when it is water it will not be as much as it is now.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|35|_: But if there is no water, etc., it invalidates. Since it receives tumah because its formation requires taharah, so wrote Perishah and Beit Yosef, that even though it is a simple wooden vessel, nevertheless since it receives tumah d'rabbanan it invalidates; and Hagahat Drishah disagreed with this, for below, seif 48, it implies that only what receives tumah d'oraisa invalidates; and so concludes Bach, that here it deals with a board on which a woman bakes bread, or joined for work, that now even if it has no rim it receives tumah — end of his words; and so Taz, that with a tray that has rims it deals, that is not a simple wooden vessel and receives tumah. And accordingly one must say that which we said above, seif 14, that even what receives tumah from rabbinic words one does not stream through it — is different; examine.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|36|א: "And if he hollowed a pit in it," etc. — one should not challenge: although they are drawn, nevertheless they come to the mikveh through drawing and drawing that was drawn is valid, as below, seif 44; and it is strained to say it deals when he hollowed the pit near the mikveh in a case where there is no drawing. And further, that a pipe narrow on both sides, etc., implies even if the pipe is very long; and one can say here it deals when he comes to bring water to a mikveh that does not have a majority of valid water, for drawing that was drawn is not valid except when the mikveh has a majority of valid water, as below — and it is simple.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|36|ג: "And wide," etc. — meaning, even though it is wide in the middle, it is not considered to receive unless he hollowed to receive pebbles in it — R' Shimshon.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|36|ד: "And if the water comes," etc., "in a wheel," etc. — so Darkei Moshe wrote: Mordechai on the wheel that rolls water, and on the wheel small pierced vessels are fixed like a water channel, and when the wheel rolls the small vessels fill and pour, etc.; Rokeach wrote that it is permitted to immerse in that case even if there is no measure of a mikveh, since the water always rises there is connection, even though the vessels are not pierced like the opening of a wineskin, since the water floats on the surface of the bucket on both sides there is connection and they are not invalid because they were drawn in vessels, for the vessels are pierced like a water channel — end of his words; and my heart wavered, end of Mordechai; and Beit Yosef wrote that all commentators disagree with this permission, that there is no connection in such a case for a mikveh, even though the water floats above on the bucket, etc., end of Darkei Moshe; and these matters are explained in Beit Yosef, this siman, and explained there that if the vessels are pierced like the opening of a wineskin it is obvious there is connection; rather there they were not pierced only like a water channel; and it is straightforward as below, seif 52. And now one should wonder at the Rav who copied these words that are only according to the one who holds a vessel pierced like a water channel is not considered a vessel; but the Rav already wrote above, seif 7, that we require a hole like the opening of a wineskin, and so below, seif 40, plainly like Tur; if so, since they are pierced here in a way that is not called a vessel, there is connection too — requires further study.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|40|ג: "And three log fell there." — after the spring lacked forty se'ah.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|40|ד: "If it is possible to plug the openings of the spring." — and to clean them easily in a way that three log of the first invalidated water will not remain at all — it is good to be stringent, etc. And Bach wrote, siman 45, that it is permitted to plug the openings of the spring even in a metal vessel that receives tumah, even for one who forbids below, seif 50, to plug with something that receives tumah; for here the plugging is only to dry the mikveh — if so; and so implies from the words of Maharshal that he brought in Drishah, below, seif 55.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|40|ה: "But if there is." — any constraint until it comes to delay so the woman cannot immerse until she is delayed and her immersion is postponed — it is not proper that she delay immersing at all, etc. — Maharik there; and so Taz.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|40|ו: "One may rely," etc. — in Shulchan Aruch it is written here and so below from Maharik, roots 55, 56; and in truth from Maharik he is more stringent even in a doubt, and where there is a doubt he wrote there to rely on the lenient if there is effort in the matter — see there; rather the Rav wrote his words according to the view of most poskim and Beit Yosef who are lenient; and similar to what Maharik wrote in a doubt, the Rav wrote in certainty and in a doubt he permitted entirely b'dieved, as Semak and most poskim; and Maharik himself in root 55 wrote so, only that afterward in root 56 he was stringent — see there.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|41|ד: "They are not considered intentional," etc. — Hagahat Drishah challenged: if so, why do we invalidate above, seif 8, in a spring what exited outside the vessel? And it is possible that above it deals when the vessel was filled intentionally — end of his words; and to me it appears that specifically for rainwater one can say it is unintentional, for the matter does not depend on him, only when rain descends from heaven; but for a spring, whenever the vessel is placed so the spring passes into it, it is always considered intentional, for necessarily the spring passes over it; and therefore these words were not said anywhere regarding a spring, only regarding rainwater, as stated.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|44|א: "Until they are half-and-half." — and all the more so a majority of drawn water that invalidates through drawing. And Bach wrote, seif 26, in the name of Ra'avad: this is specifically when he drew intentionally; but unintentionally, even entirely through drawing, is valid — see there; and see end of seif 15.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|44|ג: "If everything is found invalid." — since he filled on his shoulders directly into the mikveh and did not draw first — even so, if he afterward opened the pipe, etc., it is valid.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|44|ד: "But," etc. — meaning, he first drew drawn water to the mikveh and they are not twenty se'ah, and afterward he brought upon them a majority of valid water — meaning rainwater fell upon them more than twenty se'ah — it does not help even if he afterward opened the pipe and all were drawn to one place, for we do not say drawn water that was drawn entirely is valid except when there was initially a majority of valid water.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|46|_: Provided there was no name of a detached vessel upon it. — meaning, even though they are vessels that do not invalidate the mikveh, they do not validate the drawn water to be considered as drawn, except when there was no name of a detached vessel upon it; and here it deals when the water was fit to come to the mikveh aside from this vessel; but if they were not fit to come aside from it, even if there was no name of a detached vessel upon it, if it is a vessel that receives tumah it invalidates, because formation through taharah is required, as below, seif 48.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|47|ב: "Valid," etc. — Bach wrote: this is specifically according to the one who said above, seif 40, that a spring is not invalidated by drawing; but for us who are stringent there, the same here — end of his words. And for now there is another reason here, as Rosh wrote (from whom this law is derived) in a responsum, general principle 31, halachah 11, and so it is: because most of the strength of the water is from its place of springing; and likewise a live-water well, its springing is from roots spreading here and there under the ground; and also in time of heat and drought when their roots are cut off and their water cannot fill the well, nevertheless the moisture of the roots and water remain in them, only they are little and insufficient to fill the well; nevertheless when water comes upon them and they add water from themselves, it is found that drawing was purified through increase and drawing — end of his words; and Beit Yosef brings it. And if so, the first reason Rosh wrote there is not needed: and further, a known matter that those roots cannot remain without any water at all, and since they have some water they have the law of a spring, and a spring is not invalidated by drawing — if so. Also in Rosh's responsum it appears clear that the first reason is primary and the whole responsum is built on this reason; and it appears that even one who says drawn water that was entirely drawn is invalid concedes here for two reasons stated; and even one who invalidates drawing in a spring, even if he also holds drawn water that was entirely drawn is invalid — still, one can say he concedes here since there are two aspects for leniency: drawn water that was drawn and a spring; and so appears the view of the Rav and Taz, that here for all it is valid.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|48|א: "One who comes to draw water." — even valid water must not be, etc.; and it deals when the water is not fit to come to the mikveh except through this drawing in a vessel that receives tumah; therefore, even though it is a vessel not made to receive, since it receives tumah it invalidates; but if the water is fit to come aside from it, it does not invalidate unless it was made to receive, as above, seif 35.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|48|ב: "He should not hold in his hand a page," etc. — since a person receives tumah, but the page is a simple wooden vessel and does not receive tumah from the Torah. Ma'adanei Melech wondered, daf 311 side b: above, seif 14, the Mechaber copied Rambam's words that even in something that receives tumah from rabbinic words one does not stream through it — requires further study, end of his words. And it appears to me that streaming is different, since it is only drop by drop; and further one can say that there he only said one does not stream through it, meaning the water should not be called streaming to purify even in flowing waters, but nevertheless they are called trickling and purify in ashboran — it appears to me.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|49|א: "One who draws from a spring," etc. — and specifically while they are connected to the spring or valid mikveh; but if the spraying of what draws in the pipe was stopped, it is invalid afterward — Darkei Moshe, end of Hagahat Perishah; and I looked in Darkei Moshe and he only brought Rosh's responsum that Beit Yosef brings, and so it is: even though their formation is through tumah, it is valid since mikveh-water is connected to the spring or to another valid mikveh, for an entirely drawn mikveh is purified through hashakah, as we learned in chapter 7 of Mikvaot: they purify mikvaot — upper from lower and distant from near; how? One brings a pipe of earthenware or of reed and draws and pours hashakah, even like a hair suffices — end of his words; and Hagahat Perishah understood they are still connected and it is not necessary; one can say it only comes to teach us that hashakah helps also regarding a pipe; and if so, just as hashakah helps even if it was afterward stopped (as below, seif 52), so too here; and although one can distinguish and say a pipe is worse — nevertheless it is not necessary — examine.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|49|ב: "For we consider," etc. — and it appears to one who draws water from the spring to vessels that were invalidated, even what exits outside the vessel, above, seif 8, and their connection does not help them, for there the vessel has a receptacle and was invalidated because of drawn water, unlike here where there is only because of something that receives tumah — hashakah properly helps him — Beit Yosef and the acharonim.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|50|א: "Of rainwater." — to exclude a spring, as below.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|50|ב: "And all this is specifically," etc. — apparently he means that if it comes from a spring, even though the spring was stopped, the law of a spring is upon it to purify in flowing waters, as in Maharik; for if he comes to exclude whether it is still a spring, it is obvious; and so the language implies "it comes from a spring." But in s.k. 30 I challenged Maharik's words, for when the spring was stopped there is no longer a spring upon it; and therefore one can say here it deals that it still comes from a spring; and lest you say, since it is in a mikveh in a gathered place we should fear its streaming — he informs us.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|52|ב: "And the spraying of the water," etc. — meaning, to exclude those poskim who hold it suffices that the hole be like the opening of a wineskin even if the water spraying is not so large; rather we require the water spraying to be like the opening of a wineskin.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|52|ג: "And after the invalid was mixed," etc. — Bach wrote: specifically when invalid was mixed with non-invalid, it remains in its validity forever; but when the lacking was mixed with the complete, since the hole was plugged and behold it is lacking before us, what does it help that it was mixed initially with the complete, since it is now lacking — it should only be complete; and so is proven from the language at the beginning where he mentioned lacking and invalid, and here he only mentioned invalid — if so; and so Perishah in the name of Maharshal; and so explained in responsum of Rosh, general principle 31, halachah 2; and these matters are straightforward.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|52|ד: "Forever in its validity," etc. — and Rabbenu Yerucham wrote that commentators were uncertain whether the drawn remains in its validity or, since the hole was plugged, it returns to its invalidity as at first; and Beit Yosef and Darkei Moshe bring it; and it is good to be stringent l'chatchila.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|52|ה: "And since it is near the river." — or near a complete mikveh, so that we see seepage; but when one digs near another two or three excavations that are all lacking and none has forty se'ah, even though it is recognizable that the ground seeps and seepage spreads from one to another, there is no connection — there.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|53|א: "A drawn mikveh," etc. — for that which we require like the opening of a wineskin is specifically to validate a lacking mikveh from the complete; but to validate drawn water from a complete non-drawn mikveh, even if one only pours hashakah like a hair, it is valid, because drawn water only invalidates rabbinically and they were lenient in this. — there.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|53|ב: "Like a hair." — meaning, like a hair-thread.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|53|ג: "Valid." — Bach wondered: above, seif 7, requires like removing an olive, and so above, seif 40, a hole like a hair does not suffice to bring water by hand l'chatchila, and here he validates with a hole like a hair, like Rashba's view — requires further study, end of his words; and I do not know what the difficulty is, for Rashba himself in a responsum holds that by law above we require like the opening of a wineskin, and Beit Yosef brings it above, daf 237 side b at length; rather certainly one must distinguish, for here is different since there is a complete mikveh here, only it is drawn, and there is a complete mikveh beside it; therefore a hair suffices for mixture of mikvaot, since the drawn is rabbinic — examine.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|53|ד: "There are disputants," etc. — according to their reasons: for above, seif 3, entirely drawn is invalid d'oraisa; and accordingly, where the mikveh was mostly valid and partly drawn, such as when three log of drawn water fell in, all agree a hair suffices; and so it appears to me to answer what Bach wondered on Rosh and his supporters who require a hole like the opening of a wineskin, for we learned: they purify mikvaot, upper from lower, etc., and pour hashakah even like a hair; and he strained to reconcile that Rosh also concedes a hair suffices, only he was stringent to decree drawn on account of non-drawn, end of his words. According to what I wrote, it is simple: Rosh establishes that mishnah when the upper mikveh is invalid only rabbinically; and what Rosh wrote in a responsum as proof for the law of a spring drawn through a pipe, above, seif 49, that it is valid from the mishnah above (and I brought it above, s.k. 104), is not to say that for entirely drawn a hair suffices, rather he brings proof that even though it was drawn through a pipe that receives tumah, hashakah helps him, as explained there in the responsum — that is his intent; and so for each according to how he invalidates rabbinically with a hair and d'oraisa with like the opening of a wineskin, as stated.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|54|א: "For two it combines," etc. — and commentators disagree which is called 'two' and which 'evening'; therefore Bach wrote that for practical action they have no validity unless there is a hole like the opening of a wineskin in one place, whether in this one or that one.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|55|א: "All three were validated." — even the drawn; and it deals when the water that exited returned to its place, for otherwise they are like flowing waters and their immersion did not take effect; when the mikvaot are of rainwater; and it deals when nothing was lacking at the time water exited on their lips, such as when the mikveh walls are high; for otherwise certainly their immersion did not take effect and the mikvaot were not validated, even if they are springs, for they are lacking — all this is explained from responsum of Rivash; however it appears specifically here when the mikveh has only forty se'ah we require that they return to their place; but if they are more than forty se'ah we do not require that, for even when they flow outside, forty se'ah remain and they are not called flowing waters since through the person immersing they exit outside; and even for one who invalidates above, seif 50, when they exit through a crack, even if forty se'ah remain he concedes here that specifically there they exit by themselves not at the time of immersion he invalidates, but here from the immersion itself — and so implies somewhat from Rivash's responsum there, not like the implication from Maharik, siman 157, to invalidate in such a case — see there.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|55|ב: "They were connected together," etc. — and even if the middle one connected to drawn before connecting to valid, it is not invalidated thereby, for it also connected to valid before the drawn descended into them; and know it is so, for even when the drawn was in the middle, the valid ones were not invalidated by connecting to drawn on its lip and again descending from the drawn into them — and this is the reason: because through mixture and drawing they descended into them — Rosh.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|57|_: Provided he does not uproot, etc. — for if the wave was uprooted it would not purify, for a mikveh does not purify in flowing waters except in ashboran; and if uprooted it is not ashboran. However, specifically a mikveh that does not flow but rainwater gathered in a pit; but a mikveh that flows live water — we hold it purifies in flowing waters and in any quantity; even if the wave was uprooted it would purify vessels in any quantity, for vessels do not require forty se\'ah, and it is not similar to a wave uprooted from the sea, for we require forty se\'ah even for vessels (above, seif 5), because the sea is not considered like a spring at all to purify in flowing waters, but not to purify in any quantity as Perishah explained; but an actual spring that purifies vessels in any quantity, even if the wave was uprooted from the spring and fell on the vessel, purifies in any quantity — it appears simple, end of Bach, this siman. And it is difficult on his words, for this law is taken from Rosh, end of Niddah, who wrote there: provided he does not uproot the wave, for then it would not purify if there are not forty se\'ah in it — end of his words; and Beit Yosef brings it; and so Rabbenu Yerucham, nekudot 56, end of part 5. And therefore it must be that he deals with a spring, for if with a mikveh, even if there are forty se\'ah, what is it, since it is flowing when uprooted? And further, if with a mikveh, there is a difficulty from what he brought from Rosh from the mishnah of a wave uprooted with forty se\'ah that fell on a person and vessels — they are pure; and he wrote: this anonymous statement is like Rabbi Yosi (who holds there is law of spring upon it and purifies in flowing waters), for a wave uprooted implies even from the sea; apparently it purifies in flowing waters — end of his words. And if so, even for a wave uprooted from a mikveh he holds it purifies in flowing waters; rather certainly Rosh says here in a spring too one should not uproot, for then it will not purify if there are not forty se\'ah; and the reason is that it does not suffice in a spring in any quantity except in the body of the spring, but whatever is uprooted, although it purifies in flowing waters, nevertheless does not purify in any quantity when uprooted. And it is strained to say what Rosh wrote "if there are not forty se\'ah" refers to a person, for he did not mention a person there at all, rather a pipe placed in the cave opening; and although Rabbenu Yerucham wrote there: and so the law for immersion of a person — certainly the law is for immersion of a person that one may immerse in a wave that has forty se\'ah; but to say Rosh deals specifically with a person, this is not implied; rather it appears that even for vessels, an uprooted wave from a spring requires forty se\'ah — so it appears to me. And in Tosafot Yom Tov, end of chapter 7 of Mikvaot, he challenged Rosh: even if there are forty se\'ah, nevertheless it becomes through something that receives tumah; and so in Perishah, one can say so; however Rosh\'s view appears that it is not called becoming through something that receives tumah except when the water that becomes a mikveh passes through something that receives tumah; but here, although the person brings and conducts in the mikveh and through this the wave is uprooted, nevertheless the wave was uprooted from the mikveh itself, and at the place of its uprooting there are no human hands — examine.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|58|א: "The holes of the cave in it." — meaning: a cave is a mikveh, for such were originally most of their mikvaot in caves.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|58|ב: "In any quantity." — because they are considered part of the mikveh.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|59|א: "A depression." — it is a pit under the mikveh.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|60|א: "In a stream-bed." — meaning, in a valley.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|60|ב: "Of rainwater in it." — specifically rainwater; but a spring mixes even in flowing waters.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|62|ב: "Even though his feet are in it." — and it is not similar to a garment in the next seif, for as long as it touches him it is also considered mikveh-water, for a garment is thick and absorbs much water, unlike a person whose water is not absorbed in the essence of his limbs, only on the surface of his body; and touching in order to touch again is not connection — Rivash.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|65|ב: "She need not return and immerse again." — for we can say: establish him on his presumption, and no new impurity was born at all — there; meaning, that it was complete before us; but if it is now lacking, his immersion did not take effect, for we establish the impure on his presumption, as below, seif 71; and see in responsum of R' Lav, part 3, siman 71.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|66|א: "Whether stones, bundles of wood, or reeds." — that the water between them is not considered an interruption and they combine to forty se'ah.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|66|ב: "Provided the entire mikveh is not divided." — for then it would be like a mikveh divided with a basket and sieve, where one who immerses there, his immersion did not take effect — R' Shimshon; meaning, when there is no hole like the opening of a wineskin between them, as above, seif 52; but when there is a hole like the opening of a wineskin, it is valid.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|71|_: Whether in the public domain or in a karmelit. — meaning: even though generally we hold doubtful tumah in the public domain is pure, here we say: establish the impure person on his presumption.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|72|א: "Two mikvaot," etc. — the whole seif deals when there is a majority of valid water in the mikveh, for then there is only rabbinic doubt; but d'oraisa we do not say "I say," as I wrote above, siman 111, s.k. 14 — see there.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|72|ב: "One drawn," etc. — and the same for all other types of invalid matter that fell in invalid water.
siftei-kohen/part-002.txt|74|א: "All," etc. — invalid; and it is not similar to above, seif 39, for there the reason is the presumption of mikvaot as valid; and Rosh explained (and invalidates): one who makes a mikveh to immerse in it makes it (only) if he made it in validity; and I brought it in s.k. 144 — meaning: since initially it was a valid mikveh, therefore also now when made for a mikveh it is made; and since so, presumably it was made in validity; but here we do not know at all if it was made for a mikveh or not — it appears to me.
